tanti: tantus, -a, -um — so great, such (m. nom. pl.; n. gen. sg.)
tanto: tantus, -a, -um — so great, such (m./n. abl. sg.)

tendit: tendō, -ere, tetendī, tentum — to stretch, extend, direct one's way (3rd sg. pres.)
tenet: teneō, tenēre, tenuī, tentum — to hold, keep, occupy (3rd sg. pres.)

tenus: tenus (prep. + abl., placed after its noun) — as far as, up to
terrae: terra, -ae (f.) — earth, land, country (gen./dat. sg.; nom. pl.)
teucrum: Teucrī, -ōrum (m. pl.) — Teucrians, Trojans (gen. pl., archaic -um for -ōrum)
tibi: tū, tuī — you (sg.); tibi, to/for you (dat.)
torquet: torqueō, torquēre, torsī, tortum — to twist, whirl, hurl (3rd sg. pres.)
torrentis: torrēns, -entis — rushing, boiling, torrent-like (pres. part. of torreō; m./f. acc. pl., i-stem form; also gen. sg.)
totidem: totidem (indecl. adj.) — just as many, the same number
totum: tōtus, -a, -um — whole, entire (m. acc. sg.; n. nom./acc. sg.)
triviaeque: Trivia, -ae (f.) — Trivia, Diana/Hecate, goddess of the crossroads (gen./dat. sg.) + -que, and

truncumque: truncus, -ī (m.) — trunk, headless body (acc. sg.) + -que, and

tulit: ferō, ferre, tulī, lātum — to bear, bring, carry; sē ferre, to betake oneself (3rd sg. perf.)
tum: tum (adv.) — then, at that time; next
tuos: tuus, -a, -um — your, yours (sg. poss.) (m. acc. pl.)

turni: Turnus, -ī (m.) — Turnus, king of the Rutuli, Latinus's rival for Lavinia (gen. sg.)
turnus: Turnus, -ī (m.) — Turnus, young king of the Rutulians, suitor of Lavinia (nom. sg.)
ufens: Ūfēns, -entis (m.) — Ufens, Aequian leader; also a river of Latium (voc. sg.; nom. sg.)
umbra: umbra, -ae (f.) — shade, shadow (abl. sg.; nom. sg.)
umbrae: umbra, -ae (f.) — shadow, shade (nom. pl.; gen./dat. sg.)
umbro: Umbro, -ōnis (m.) — Umbro, Marsian priest and healer (nom. sg.)
una: ūnus, -a, -um — one, a single (f. abl./nom. sg.); ūnā (adv.), together · also ūnā, adv., once (satis ūnā superque, enough once and more)

versis: vertō, -ere, vertī, versum — to turn, change (perf. pass. part., m./n. abl./dat. pl.)

vir: vir, virī (m.) — man, hero, husband (nom. sg.)

volcente: Volcens (Volscens), -entis (m.) — Volcens, Latin captain of horse (abl. sg.)
volvitur: volvō, volvere, volvī, volūtum — to roll, tumble (3rd sg. pres. pass.)
